title: HB1301 (2024 Regular): Wearing, Carrying, or Transporting Firearms – Business Sign Posting Requirements

provenance.fetched_by: Open States bulk data (Maryland) (gun-policy Stage 5, Maryland); operative text read by a Sonnet fill agent from the official Mississippi text (First Reader; official copy, https://mgaleg.maryland.gov/2024RS/bills/hb/hb1301f.pdf)
provenance.note: First reader (as filed); no passage vote recorded. The rest of the bill renumbers existing subsections and cross-references.

operative_text:
Section 1 (Md. Code Ann., Criminal Law § 4–111(f)): (F) (1) A BUSINESS THAT DOES NOT WANT FIREARMS ON THE BUSINESS’S PROPERTY SHALL POST A CLEAR AND CONSPICUOUS SIGN AT THE MAIN OR ANY SECONDARY ENTRANCE OF THE BUSINESS AT LEAST 24 INCHES FROM THE EDGE OF THE ENTRYWAY AND 4 FEET OFF THE GROUND, THAT: (I) STATES THAT IT IS NOT PERMISSIBLE TO WEAR, CARRY, OR TRANSPORT A FIREARM ON THE BUSINESS’S PROPERTY; AND (II) IS AT LEAST 12 INCHES WIDE BY 18 INCHES LONG. (2) IF THE BUSINESS IS A PRIVATE BUSINESS, THE SIGN REQUIRED UNDER PARAGRAPH (1) OF THIS SUBSECTION SHALL ALSO INCLUDE THE BUSINESS’S ADDRESS CLEARLY AND CONSPICUOUSLY ON THE FRONT OF THE SIGN.
Section 1 (Md. Code Ann., Criminal Law § 4–111(a)(3)): “BUSINESS” MEANS AN ORGANIZATION OR ENTERPRISING ENTITY THAT ENGAGES IN PROFESSIONAL, COMMERCIAL, OR INDUSTRIAL ACTIVITIES.
